answer: Adversarial decoy-answer injection resists sybil graders: the system occasionally injects a known-flawed answer crafted to look superficially strong, and a grader that passes the hidden flaw is caught rubber-stamping. A ring grading its own members at the forge of collusion fails these decoys at a rate honest careful graders never match — the delta between a cluster's decoy-failure rate and the honest baseline across the meadow is the detection signal. Graders who repeatedly miss injected flaws lose standing, pricing out lazy or colluding grading.
